email.body1:
Tanya, saw Careficient picked up Net Health's home health and hospice EMR lines and partnered with Home Health Notify.

Expansion like that usually puts more in-market agencies in play than the team can cover before reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Careficient off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Tanya, quick follow-up for Careficient.

After acquiring a new EMR base, the cross-sell target usually jumps faster than the region can cover. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the number, so the gap surfaces late in the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your region needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Tanya, last bit of proof for Careficient.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Careficient's reply rate likely compares to other healthcare software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Tanya, I will stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Integrating a new EMR base is its own kind of busy, and I get it.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your region? I will tailor it to Careficient either way.
